deities: Hazrat Shahpeer (Sufi saint interred here; not a Hindu deity)

history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Sufi Muslim dargah (mausoleum), built in 1628 by Mughal Empress Nur Jahan in honour of Hazrat Shahpeer, said to have been a teacher of Emperor Jahangir and physician/advisor to the queen. Built of red sandstone with Mughal-style carvings, jali work and floral motifs, its most distinctive feature is the missing dome: historians believe construction was left unfinished after the saint's death. The Archaeological Survey of India recognises it as a protected national monument. It stands near Suraj Kund / Shohrab Gate on Garh Road, Meerut, and draws both devotees and heritage tourists.

name: Shapir ki Dargah
town_description: Meerut, in the Doab region of western Uttar Pradesh, is one of India's oldest continuously inhabited cities — tradition names it as the birthplace of three Jain Tirthankaras — and the 1857 uprising against the British began in its cantonment. Today it is a major commercial and sporting-goods manufacturing centre. Its heritage sites include the Shapir/Shahpeer Dargah, Mustafa Castle and the Chandi Devi temple, famous for the annual Nauchandi fair after Holi.

travel.airport: Meerut has no commercial airport; nearest major airport is Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, roughly 100 km away
travel.road: Garh Road / Shohrab Gate area of Meerut, connected by NH-34 and other state highways
